title: Macroscopic position-position entanglement by photon recoil in Rydberg atoms
abstract: Entanglement between two spatially separate matter particles can be generated via many means and often resides in the internal states of particles. Here, via Rydberg blockade in two spatially separate neutral atoms, we find that the photon recoil in Rydberg excitation can push one atom microns away provided the other atom exerts a state-dependent Rydberg-mediated blockade. When the atoms are recaptured by optical traps, a position-position entangled state between two spatially separate atoms can emerge. This realizes a Bell state of two atoms, where the entanglement exists in the position of each atom and the distance between the two possible locations of each atom can be in the hundred-micron regime.
summary: This paper reports a method to generate position-position entangled states between two spatially separated neutral atoms. The technique relies on exploiting photon recoil during Rydberg excitation, which imparts a measurable momentum kick leading to macroscopic separation ($\ell$). This work advances the use of atomic arrays for quantum state engineering beyond internal qubit degrees of freedom.
main_problem: The primary goal is generating macroscopic entanglement between two spatially separated neutral atoms.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrate the deterministic generation of position-position entangled states between two atoms, with separations reaching the micron scale via photon recoil during Rydberg excitation.
method: The process utilizes controlled Rydberg blockade interactions in two separate atoms to induce a momentum kick on one atom. This kick translates into measurable spatial separation after free flight and subsequent recapture by optical traps.
model_or_system: The system involves two spatially separated neutral atoms (e.g., Rubidium) trapped in optical tweezers, leveraging the strong, state-dependent interactions mediated by Rydberg excitation. The dynamics are governed by time-dependent Hamiltonians incorporating blockade potentials and photon recoil momentum kicks.
key_observables: Position separation ($\ell$), Entanglement Fidelity ($F$), Population Restoration ($p(t)$), and the resulting entangled state $|\Psi_{ct}angle$.
important_parameters: The achievable position separation $\ell$ can reach several microns, with enhancements possible using lighter atoms like ${^3	ext{He}^*}$. The process efficiency is limited by internal state coherence time ($T_1$).
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include the unit efficiency of recapturing the atomic wavepacket and analyzing the impact of Doppler dephasing and Rydberg-state decay.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but the context implies figures showing entanglement fidelity vs. time/cycles, and position distributions demonstrating spatial separation.
paper_structure: The paper details the physical mechanism involving Rydberg blockade to generate momentum kicks, analyzes the resulting entangled state evolution over free flight time $T$, discusses enhancements via multiple Rabi cycles ($N$), and evaluates performance against decoherence sources like Doppler effects.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses creating macroscopic quantum correlations (position entanglement) using established AMO tools (Rydberg blockade), pushing the boundaries from internal-state qubits to spatial degrees of freedom in cold atom systems.
